title: After disasters
hook: Sikh volunteers cook and clean after floods and fires
tomorrow: the fire's out. the hills are black. who plants them back?

segments.voice: Yesterday, teaching as seva: teach freely; a kitchen table is a classroom. Dev got three fractions right. Then the sky turned orange.

A wildfire is burning in the hills two towns over. At noon the sky is orange and smells like a campfire nobody wanted. Harjit's trucks are loading pallets of water for the evacuation center at a high school gym. Simran rides along. When they pull in, Sikh volunteers have already set up gas burners in the parking lot. Big pots. Dal, rice, roti, tea. A sign in marker: free hot food, everyone welcome.
screen: `AN ORANGE SKY AT NOON.` → `HARJIT'S TRUCKS, LOADED WITH WATER.` → `FREE HOT FOOD, EVERYONE WELCOME.`

segments.voice: Sikh volunteers have cooked and cleaned after floods and fires, and the reason is an old one on this path: langar doesn't ask who you are. Ardas, as the Sikh code of conduct gives it, ends with a phrase that holds the whole idea: sarbat da bhala, the good of all. Not the good of Sikhs. The good of all. So after a disaster, the seva is mostly simple. Show up. Bring what you have: water, a pot, a truck, two hands. Ask what's needed instead of guessing. Stay after the cameras leave. And look how this whole week fits into one parking lot. Start at home: Harjit's own trucks. Beyond the walls: a gym full of strangers. Langar everywhere: the pots on the burners. Sit with them: Bebe on a folding chair beside a man whose street was evacuated. Company for the old: she doesn't leave him. Teach freely: Dev, who came with Kiran, showing a younger kid how to fold napkins. And, today, show up.
screen: `LANGAR DOESN'T ASK WHO YOU ARE.` · `SARBAT DA BHALA: THE GOOD OF ALL.` · `BRING WHAT YOU HAVE. ASK. STAY.` · `A WEEK OF SEVA IN ONE PARKING LOT.` · then, large: `SHOW UP.`

segments.voice: Name one kind of emergency that could reach your town: a fire, a flood, a storm, a long power cut. Name one thing you could bring or do if it came, and the one obstacle most likely to stop you. Then choose one small step past that obstacle, and let it rest while you sit.
After disasters. Seva when floods and fires come: showing up for the good of all. Sarbat da bhala.
Your line: show up. Water, a pot, two hands, for the good of all. Next week, more seva.
